original_question: For the same incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid problem, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of the trajectory attractor and of the global attractor without imposing restrictions on the coefficients, external force, or initial data, in dimensions n ≥ 2?
target_in_paper: The attractor open problem in the review’s discussion of the autonomous Jeffreys-type viscoelastic-fluid equations: after reviewing existence of a minimal trajectory attractor and the induced global attractor under restrictive hypotheses, the remaining paper-faithful question is whether one can obtain Hausdorff-dimension estimates for those attractors, and whether the attractor theory can be developed without the special restrictions on coefficients/force/data used in the known theorem.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the model class (incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid), the dynamical objects of interest (trajectory attractor and global attractor), the geometric quantity to be estimated (Hausdorff dimension), and the paper’s concern with removing restrictive assumptions on coefficients, forcing, and initial data. The ambient dimension n >= 2 is also consistent with the way the authors formulate the motion problem for a bounded domain in R^n.
missing_details: The paper’s attractor discussion distinguishes the autonomous problem from the non-autonomous one; your draft should explicitly say autonomous (time-independent external force) if that is the intended target.
The setting is an initial-boundary value problem in a bounded sufficiently smooth domain Omega subset of R^n, not the whole space.
The attractors are those of weak-solution trajectory spaces; the paper’s autonomous object is a minimal trajectory attractor together with the corresponding global attractor generated by it.

The restrictions to be removed are not arbitrary: they are the special hypotheses used in the reviewed existence theorem, especially coefficient restrictions needed to derive the exponential/energy estimates that make the attractor construction work.
The external force should be identified as the stationary body force entering the autonomous problem, rather than an unspecified forcing term.
The initial data should be understood as the data in the weak-solution phase space used for the Jeffreys problem reviewed by the paper, not arbitrary rough data in an unspecified space.
The question is about finiteness/upper estimation of Hausdorff dimension of the attractors, not necessarily computing the exact dimension.
Your draft does not name the boundary condition (the standard homogeneous Dirichlet/no-slip condition on the velocity in the reviewed bounded-domain problem).

Your draft does not make clear that the paper separately reviews the non-autonomous uniform-attractor theory; that distinction should be suppressed only if one explicitly says the target is the autonomous attractor result.
refined_question: For the autonomous initial-boundary value problem for the incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium considered in the paper—posed in a bounded sufficiently smooth domain Omega subset of R^n, n >= 2, with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition and time-independent body force—can one prove that the minimal trajectory attractor of weak solutions and the corresponding global attractor have finite Hausdorff dimension, and can this be done without the special restrictions on the Jeffreys coefficients, the external force, and the initial data that are imposed in the reviewed attractor-existence theorem?
justification: The draft is close, but it is not yet stand-alone in the paper’s sense. The review separates autonomous and non-autonomous attractor results, so the autonomous setting must be named explicitly. It also works in the weak-solution framework for a bounded-domain initial-boundary value problem and reviews existence of a minimal trajectory attractor and the induced global attractor only under additional hypotheses needed for dissipative/exponential estimates. The sharpened question therefore needs to identify the autonomous bounded-domain Jeffreys problem, the weak-solution attractors involved, and the fact that the intended improvement is finite-Hausdorff-dimension control together with removal of the restrictive coefficient/forcing/data assumptions. Because the arXiv HTML exposes only the abstract, I cross-checked the attractor material against the authors’ detailed monograph exposition of the same Jeffreys-model attractor theory.
